title: Completion of remote and centre-based cardiac rehabilitation: a retrospective comparison with a single completion definition
abstract: Objective: to compare completion between remote and centre-based cardiac rehabilitation when one definition and full denominators are used. Design: retrospective comparison of programme records for 1,146 referrals, 2023 to 2025. Analysis: adjusted risk difference with an E-value, and results by sex, age, deprivation and distance. Results and conclusions will follow the analysis.
introduction: Published comparisons of rehabilitation settings disagree, partly because completion is defined differently between programmes. A cited regional comparison has since been corrected by its authors, which is why the local analysis fixes one definition before extraction.
methods: All referrals who chose a programme are included, with non-starters in both denominators. Completion is 12 of 16 sessions or 6 of 8 coaching weeks. A log-binomial model adjusts for five referral factors.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present uptake and completion by programme and by group, the adjusted difference and the E-value.
discussion: The discussion will weigh the adjusted difference against confounding by choice and state whether a remote default would leave any group worse off.
limitations: Confounding by choice; unrecorded employment and car access; one programme.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not claim that one setting causes better completion.
summary: STROBE and RECORD structured draft; the introduction notes the corrected source.
